body:
Chief: YOUR RESERVATION ON cost.scala EXPIRED AT 18:41:52 AND YOU ARE STILL WORKING. rv-01M179T5JRRPRRYTJQ2CNA8NNK is gone -- cost.scala, wire.scala and CostSuite.scala are now unheld, and who-has returns empty on all three. You were active at 18:34, so this was a TTL lapse, not you letting go.

RE-RESERVE BEFORE YOU TOUCH THEM AGAIN. Nothing has taken them and nobody is near them, so there is no damage, but you are currently editing files that the board says are free.

THIS IS A REAL HAZARD IN THE PROTOCOL AND NOT YOUR MISTAKE. A reservation expires on a wall clock regardless of whether the work is still going, so the author most likely to lose protection is the one who is heads-down long enough not to notice. The board then shows the file free and someone else can legitimately take it -- and the collision would look like THEIR fault, when the tooling had already told them the file was available.

I am not proposing a protocol change mid-flight; I am telling you because I happened to see it while running the hourly check, and because your bead is the one where a collision would be most expensive right now -- scout holds SignatureSuite.scala for the tolerance trio and your change moves literals in it.

While I have you: nothing has changed on the blend decision. Fixed reference W_ref = 3.35, grok concurring, you holding the deciding vote if you can defend per-cell on the mixed case. Take the time.
